name: Meeting Reminders
tagline: Sends automatic reminders so people actually show up to their meetings on time.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Underneath the product is a loop any agent can write: poll a calendar, find events starting soon, send a message. There is no proprietary data, no model, no network you need to join. The interesting part of the commercial version is nudging other attendees, which needs either a shared chat workspace or their consent, and that is where a personal build stops being equivalent. For reminding yourself, or a team that already lives in one Slack channel with one bot token, a single script and a cron entry covers it. The rest is onboarding polish and someone else keeping the poller alive.
coreLoopDIY: Polls your Google Calendar every minute and posts a reminder to Slack or your phone a set number of minutes before each meeting, once per event.
requirements: Google Cloud project with Calendar API enabled and OAuth client credentials
A machine that stays on: a small VPS, a Raspberry Pi, or a scheduled cloud function
A Slack incoming webhook or an ntfy topic for delivery
whatYouLose: Pinging other attendees without each of them authorizing your script or joining your Slack workspace
Someone else guaranteeing the poller ran at 8:59am when your laptop was asleep
Handling for the messy cases: recurring event exceptions, timezone shifts, declined invites, all-day events
Native mobile push and a settings UI instead of editing a config file
Team-level admin, per-person preferences, and billing if you ever wanted colleagues on it
moatNotes: The moat is calendar and chat plumbing that already works plus the fact that nobody wants to babysit a cron job for a reminder.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a reminder tool that misses a reminder is worse than no tool, and self-hosted cron jobs fail quietly. Paying also solves the social problem: you can nudge the whole meeting without asking five colleagues to grant OAuth scopes to a script you wrote on a Saturday. The software is trivial; the reliability and the permission story are what you are actually buying.
notes: A genuinely small piece of software wrapped around a genuinely annoying human problem.
prompt:
Build a personal meeting reminder daemon in an empty folder.

Stack, no alternatives: Node 20, TypeScript, tsx for running, SQLite via better-sqlite3, node-cron for scheduling. No web framework, no frontend, no database server, no telemetry, no accounts.

Behavior:
1. On first run, do a Google OAuth desktop flow for the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly, print the consent URL to the terminal, accept the pasted code, and store the refresh token in a local file token.json that is gitignored.
2. Every 60 seconds, list events from the primary calendar in a window from now to now plus 60 minutes, using the Calendar API with singleEvents true and orderBy startTime.
3. For each event, compute the reminder time as start minus LEAD_MINUTES from .env (default 5). If that moment has passed within the last 90 seconds and no reminder row exists for that event id plus start time in SQLite, send a reminder and insert the row.
4. Skip events where the user's own responseStatus is declined, events marked all-day, and events with no attendees other than the user if IGNORE_SOLO is true.
5. Delivery: post to SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL if set, otherwise POST to an ntfy topic at NTFY_URL. Message includes the title, minutes until start, the location or hangoutLink, and the attendee count.
6. Log every send and every skip reason to stdout with timestamps.

In scope: dedupe across restarts, timezone-correct math using the event's own timezone offsets, retry a failed send up to 3 times with backoff, a --dry-run flag that prints instead of sending, a --once flag for use with system cron instead of the built-in loop.

Out of scope: reminding other attendees, a web UI, multi-user support, Outlook, recurring-event edit handling beyond what singleEvents gives you.

All secrets in .env, read with process.env, no hardcoded values. Write a README with the Google Cloud setup steps, a sample .env, and a systemd unit file for running it as a service.
